newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL rubber prices close mixed on currency factor.
newsitem.headline: KL rubber prices close mixed on currency factor.

text.p: Malaysia's rubber market closed mixed on Tuesday with players watching movements of the ringgit to fix prices while the market drifted aimlessly, traders said.
There was no news of business in the market, although inquiries were reported from China for the SMR20, said the traders.
"The ringgit seems to be providing the only reao direction to the market now," said a trader.
At 1000GMT, the ringgit was at 2.7850 to a dollar in Kuala Lumpur.
The Malaysian currency had weakened more than 13 percent against the dollar since last July, providing much advantage to commodity exporters, but has been consolidating in the last week.

Traders said on Monday that buyers could be looking at the Jakarta rubber market because the rupiah had fallen more drastically than the ringgit since last week, making prices of Indonesian rubber more attractive.
At the close, the RSS1 for September buyer in Kuala Lumpur's rubber market was quoted at 251 Malaysian cents (90 cents U.S.) a kg, down half cent from Monday.
The SMR20 for September buyer was priced a cent higher at 250.50 cents a kg.
Traders were offering the SMR 20 at 249 cents a kg, the SMR CV at 289 cents, SMR L at 270, SMR 5 at 262, SMR 10 at 250 and drum latex at 192 for Aug/Sept.
